newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to maintain firm clip.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to maintain firm clip.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, whipped up by volatility due to options and futures expiries and a Dow .DJI looking set to extend Friday's 40-point gain, is expected to maintain its firm pace ahead in coming weeks, dealers said.
The Bel-20 share index .BFX closed up 0.89 percent, or 16.55 points, to 1,8895.13 in heavy trade.

"Where is the volume coming from? I don't know, I expected December to be quiet with investors on the sidelines," said one trader. "The words of Alan Greenspan have been completely forgotten, and that was only two weeks ago". Greenspan said then that assets were overvalued, sparking a sharp sell-off.

Dealers said that as this was the last trading day on Belfox futures market of the current series of Bel-20 index options and futures, volume had been expected to be as high as it had been in November, but they were bemused at its actual size.
Volume of Belgian shares traded was 6.9 billion francs, almost the double of yesterday's already chunky 3.5 billion.

Dealers said Wall Street's renewed energy, closing 127 points higher on Thursday and seeing further gains on Friday, had caused investors to shrug off speculation that the U.S. market was in imminent trouble.
